briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 3, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis Warning and Urgency of Response
sections.content: The UN has warned that the record-breaking El Niño climate phenomenon is 'growing before our eyes' and is expected to be the largest in at least 1,000 years [91]. Meanwhile, in Nepal, search operations for flood victims have been ongoing for three days without success. With recovery costs estimated at over $4 billion, nine employees of a South Korean company have been missing for a week [83, 84, 87, 89]. Furthermore, Arctic habitats such as the 'North Water' region between Canada and Greenland are experiencing increased threats to ice due to global warming [95], and Australia's newly established environmental protection agency has drawn the ire of climate organizations by approving a coal project [93]. Amidst these crises, some media outlets have shown a climate change-denying stance regarding record-breaking heatwave warnings, exacerbating controversy despite thousands of heat-related deaths [92].

sections.title: 🌱 Republic of Korea: Accelerating Carbon Neutrality Transition Efforts and Challenges
sections.content: In the National Assembly, amendments to the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act and the enactment of the Climate Adaptation Act were passed, strengthening the policy foundation for climate crisis response [25, 37]. Nationwide, efforts from various entities are continuing, including Busan Jung-gu's carbon neutrality practice campaign [1, 18], Hwaseong Special City's 2030 carbon neutrality declaration and plan to quadruple renewable energy facilities [7], Nowon-gu's carbon neutrality citizen declaration [14], Changwon City's carbon neutrality education for farmers [13], and Korea Western Power's awards for a public carbon neutrality idea contest and review for commercialization [2, 3, 4, 9, 19, 21, 22, 24, 27, 30, 31]. Notably, the Korea Green Foundation and Evezary supported the Seoul International Environmental Film Festival in achieving carbon neutrality for two consecutive years through carbon credit donations [8, 12, 15, 26, 34], and Hankook Tire is accelerating its carbon neutrality efforts by establishing solar power facilities at its Geumsan plant [29, 38, 73, 75, 79, 80]. However, despite 78% of carbon-neutral city plans targeting 'all regions,' actual projects are concentrated in only a few areas, indicating remaining challenges for effective carbon neutrality implementation [10].

sections.title: ⚠️ Renewable Energy Transition: Domestic and International Expansion and Remaining Challenges
sections.content: The Ministry of Climate plans to invest approximately 10 trillion KRW in the power grid and renewable energy sectors in next year's budget [44], and five public power generation companies will be unified under 'Korea Power,' with a separate renewable energy headquarters established, signaling an all-out effort for domestic renewable energy transition [45, 63, 68]. Furthermore, Gyeongnam Province is implementing the nation's first 'solar virtuous cycle' model, utilizing profits from expanded solar power in industrial complexes for senior welfare [41, 74, 77, 78], and Pohang City and Amon Energy have signed a memorandum of understanding for a 20 billion KRW new and renewable energy project, demonstrating active regional efforts to expand renewable energy [65]. However, according to the Korea Social Responsibility Investment Forum, the renewable energy usage rate in domestic RE100 workplaces is only 13%, a significant gap compared to Japan's 90% [42, 47, 59], and in response to increased electricity demand due to semiconductor industry growth, Pyeongtaek civil society is strongly advocating for local production and consumption of renewable energy [46, 49, 69]. Internationally, China is pursuing large-scale solar power generation, dubbed the 'Great Wall of Solar,' reshaping its energy landscape [70], and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is accelerating its global renewable energy transition by increasing its clean energy generation target to 35% and promoting solar power and battery expansion [62].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating EV Transition Contributes to Carbon Emission Reduction
sections.content: The Ministry of Climate, Energy, and Environment is promoting the widespread adoption of electric vehicles by implementing a policy that offers up to a 32% discount on public EV fast-charging fees during daytime hours on weekends and holidays [86]. Hyundai Mobis is strengthening its position in the global EV market by operating a new production plant for electric vehicle powertrain systems (PE systems) in Slovakia, Europe [90]. According to an analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) in Finland, China's accelerated electrification has led to a 9% reduction in oil consumption and a 1% decrease in carbon emissions [88, 96]. This is interpreted as a positive signal, offering hope for China's decarbonization transition even amidst the Iran war situation [94].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the efforts of various nations towards carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition amidst the global climate crisis. Alongside urgent climate crisis response, tangible carbon reduction efforts must continue. This concludes today's climate briefing.
